claims.text: Service exposure causes initially single-phase HEAs to form secondary brittle phases at grain boundaries or within grains.
Formation of secondary brittle phases governs the loss of toughness and transition to brittle fracture.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can provide a homogeneous, single-phase, high-toughness initial state.
Prolonged mechanical loading and/or thermal exposure can drive phase evolution in the alloy.
Exposure at approximately 600°C, high strain rate, or cyclic fatigue for sufficient duration may produce secondary phases.
The relevant secondary phases may be intermetallic compounds or ordered precipitates.
The secondary phases are less ductile than the solid-solution matrix.
Secondary phases act as preferential sites for crack nucleation and propagation.
Crack initiation and propagation at secondary phases reduce the alloy's capacity for plastic deformation.
Reduced plastic deformation caused by secondary phases lowers fracture toughness.
Service-exposed specimens will exhibit more than a 30% reduction in fracture toughness relative to the as-prepared baseline.
Service-exposed specimens will exhibit an increased frequency of intergranular or transgranular brittle-fracture features.
Secondary phases will be detectable in the exposed specimens by microstructural analysis.
The as-prepared single-phase baseline has high fracture toughness and a ductile fracture morphology.
The hypothesis applies only when service temperature or loading conditions are sufficient to drive phase separation or precipitation.
The magnitude of toughness loss depends on the volume fraction and spatial distribution of brittle phases.
The identity and formation kinetics of secondary phases vary with alloy composition and service conditions.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes alloys that remain single-phase under service conditions, while the falsification rule treats retention of a single-phase structure with unchanged toughness as falsification. Thus, the proposed null result is simultaneously declared outside the hypothesis's applicability and decisive against it.
